title: AI Monster Generator: Create and Animate Creatures
summary: Design a monster with an AI monster generator, then make it move: real creature clips from Flick films with their exact prompts, and four steps. Start free.
body_markdown:
### What is an AI monster generator?


An AI monster generator is a tool that makes a picture or video of a monster or creature from a text prompt, a drawing or both. Flick is built for films, so the same monster can be designed as a sheet and then cast in many shots on one canvas.


### Can I make an AI monster for free?


Yes, you can start free: you get 100 credits when you sign up, 200 more for joining the Flick Discord, and 100 credits every week. Monster sheets with Nano Banana Pro and video with MiniMax H3 Max run on the free plan, while Seedance 2.0 needs the Standard plan ($20 a month).


### Can I turn my own monster drawing into a video?


Yes. Upload the drawing to a Flick canvas and cite it as a reference in a reference to video clip, or use it as the start frame of an image to video clip. The creature sheets in the residency film Xenogenesis were uploaded and cited this way.


### How do I keep the same monster in every shot?


Make one reference sheet of the monster with front, side and back views, and cite it by name in every prompt that shows it. Tusk Hunters, a film from the Flick residency, cited its monster's design sheet in 23 of its 36 monster clips.


### How do I make an AI monster scary instead of silly?


Show less of it and let sound and light do the work: describe fog, a single cold light and the noises it makes before the full creature is seen. 32 of the 36 monster clips in Tusk Hunters describe both fog and the monster's sound.


### Can I give my monster a strange detail that stays put?


Yes. Write an identity lock that names the detail, says exactly where it is, and tells the model not to change it. Xenogenesis did this for a creature with two different eye colours, naming which eye is which in 18 of its creature clips.


### Which AI models can I use for monster videos in Flick?


The clips here were made with Seedance 2.0 on the Standard plan, from sheets made with Nano Banana Pro, Nano Banana 2 and GPT Image 2. Flick also runs Seedance 2.5 and Kling 3.0 Pro, and you can mix models across the shots of one film.
